name: Robots Beyond Earth: Probes, Landers and Rovers
description: Machines without crews have visited every planet. Follow the flybys, landings and rovers that taught us what the other worlds of our Solar System are like.

checkpoints.name: First reach
checkpoints.note: Sputnik and Explorer 1 showed that machines could orbit Earth. Soon probes headed for other worlds, and in 1965 Mariner 4 sent back the first close pictures of Mars, a cratered and dry surface.

checkpoints.name: Landers and flybys
checkpoints.note: Luna 9 touched down softly on the Moon, Venera 7 sent a signal from the surface of another planet, and Lunokhod 1 drove across lunar soil. Pioneer 10 crossed the asteroid belt on its way to the giant planets, and Viking landed on Mars.

checkpoints.name: The grand tour
checkpoints.note: The Voyager twins used a rare alignment to visit the giant planets, with Voyager 2 reaching Uranus and Neptune. Galileo went to Jupiter, and late in 1996 Mars Pathfinder set off carrying the little Sojourner rover.

checkpoints.name: Orbiters and early rovers
checkpoints.note: Sojourner roamed Mars in 1997. Cassini and its Huygens lander explored the Saturn system, Spirit and Opportunity found traces of old water on Mars, Rosetta chased a comet, and New Horizons set out for the far edge of the Solar System.

checkpoints.name: The rover age
checkpoints.note: Curiosity and Perseverance act as robot geologists on Mars. New Horizons flew past the outer Solar System's dwarf worlds in 2015, and China's Chang'e 4 and India's Chandrayaan-3 made new landings on the Moon.
